entries.title: MEC-01 Decision log with dissent
entries.summary: Capture high-stakes calls, dissenting views, and follow-ups so governance stays legible to teams and impacted people.
cues: Record why options were ruled out and who was consulted.
Attach plain-language summaries for external readers.
Set a review date tied to the stewardship window.
steps: Log the decision, rejected options, and who was consulted in one place.
Attach a short summary alongside the canonical record for external readers.
Set a review date with a clear owner tied to the stewardship window.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-01 Decision log with dissent)
- Maintain a decision log for high-stakes changes with dissenting views and a dated review owner.
- Store the log in a shared system of record and retain links in audit and incident records.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/decision-log
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-01)
- Every high-stakes automated decision emits a decision-log entry ID in the receipt.
- The UI links to a plain-language summary within two clicks of the decision outcome.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-01)
[ ] Decision log entries include owner, dissent, and review date.
[ ] Plain-language summaries are attached and shareable.
[ ] Stewardship reviews were completed on schedule.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-01)
Trigger review if a high-stakes decision ships without a logged entry or dissent record.

artifacts.name: Decision record template
artifacts.purpose: Captures the decision, dissent, and follow-ups with owners.

artifacts.name: Plain-language summary
artifacts.purpose: One-paragraph recap teams can paste into briefs or release notes without jargon.

artifacts.name: Stewardship calendar entry
artifacts.purpose: Review reminder aligned to maintenance or appeal windows.

example.title: Recording a launch gate call
example.description: A cross-functional team logs why an automation launch was delayed, notes dissent from support leads, links the appeal path, and schedules a stewardship review in six weeks.

antiPatterns.title: Logs without dissent
antiPatterns.failure: Records the decision but omits rejected options and dissenting views.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Decision logs include rejected options, dissent, and a dated review owner.
antiPatterns.warning: If no dissent exists, log the absence explicitly so future reviewers can see it was considered.

antiPatterns.title: Out-of-band records
antiPatterns.failure: Keeps accountability logs in private documents that impacted teams cannot access.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Logs live in the canonical record with a shareable receipt link.
antiPatterns.warning: Sensitive data can be redacted, but the receipt must remain referenceable.

entries.title: MEC-02 Progressive consent prompts
entries.summary: Stage requests for data or automation over time, with reminders and exits that honor the consent journey.
cues: Pair each ask with why it is needed and how to revoke it.
Show impacts of opting out before a person commits.
Include a safety valve that defaults to privacy-preserving behavior.
steps: Break large asks into small prompts that explain why each is needed.
Preview what happens if someone opts out and keep the path visible.
Offer a safety valve that defaults to privacy-preserving behavior.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-02 Progressive consent prompts)
- Stage consent requests with clear revocation paths and visible opt-out impacts.
- Document safety-valve defaults that preserve privacy when consent is withheld.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/progressive-consent
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-02)
- Each consent request includes purpose, duration, and revocation instructions.
- Opt-out paths remain visible and do not degrade core safety access.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-02)
[ ] Consent journey map shows each ask, rationale, and rollback path.
[ ] Opt-out copy kit deployed across UI, email, and help surfaces.
[ ] Safety-valve defaults verified in staging and production.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-02)
Trigger review if opt-out actions fail, are ignored, or re-enable without notice.

artifacts.name: Consent journey map
artifacts.purpose: Shows each request, rationale, and rollback path across the flow.

artifacts.name: Opt-out copy kit
artifacts.purpose: Short blurbs teams reuse in UI states, emails, and help docs.

artifacts.name: Safety valve checklist
artifacts.purpose: Confirms every step has a reversible, privacy-first fallback before shipping.

example.title: Piloting a model-powered assistant
example.description: Product and legal teams stage data collection prompts over several sessions, preview how opting out affects recommendations, and keep a global “pause automation” control visible in the UI.

antiPatterns.title: One-shot consent bundles
antiPatterns.failure: Asks for every permission at once without explaining timing or scope.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Requests are staged with clear rationale, timing, and reversible defaults.
antiPatterns.warning: Bundling can be acceptable if the scope is minimal and opt-outs are explicit.

antiPatterns.title: Opt-out that does not stick
antiPatterns.failure: Offers a toggle but automation continues or re-enables without notice.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Opt-outs pause automation and are logged with a visible confirmation.
antiPatterns.warning: Some baseline data use can remain if it is disclosed and required for service safety.

entries.title: MEC-03 Maintenance windowing
entries.summary: Schedule improvements, monitoring, and resourcing using a visible stewardship window.
cues: Set owners and success criteria for each window.
Map communication cadences to risk levels and audiences.
Align dependencies so a degraded tool has a safe fallback.
steps: Define maintenance windows with owners, success criteria, and rollbacks.
Publish communication cadences by risk level and audience.
Check dependencies so degraded modes route to safe fallbacks.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-03 Maintenance windowing)
- Publish stewardship windows with named owners, success criteria, and rollback authority.
- Require comms cadences by risk tier before shipping changes.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/maintenance-windowing
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-03)
- Release plans include a window ID and owner in change tickets.
- Status updates and fallback behavior are visible to affected users.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-03)
[ ] Window calendar lists owners, coverage, and success criteria.
[ ] Comms templates are published by risk level and audience.
[ ] Fallback matrix confirms safe degraded modes for dependencies.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-03)
Trigger review if changes ship outside the stewardship window or without comms.

artifacts.name: Window calendar
artifacts.purpose: Shared schedule with owners, coverage, and success criteria.

artifacts.name: Comms templates
artifacts.purpose: Prewritten updates for high, medium, and low-risk changes tied to roles.

artifacts.name: Fallback matrix
artifacts.purpose: Lists degraded modes and who is paged when dependencies fail.

example.title: Coordinating a stewardship sprint
example.description: Engineering and operations publish a two-week window with a fallback matrix, schedule status updates by audience, and rehearse degraded-mode protocols before shipping changes.

antiPatterns.title: Stewardship without owners
antiPatterns.failure: Publishes a maintenance window without naming accountable owners or success criteria.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Each window has a named owner, success criteria, and rollback authority.
antiPatterns.warning: Shared ownership is fine if responsibilities are explicit and visible.

antiPatterns.title: Silent maintenance
antiPatterns.failure: Ships changes without comms or status updates, leaving users unaware of risks.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Comms are published by audience and risk tier, with fallback coverage noted.
antiPatterns.warning: Emergency patches can shorten comms, but they still require an after-action log.

entries.title: MEC-04 The Hard Clock
entries.summary: Give every system state a declared maximum duration so nothing sits in pending forever without escalation, expiry, or an exit.
cues: Declare the maximum duration of each state before people commit to the process.
Decide in advance whether expiry fails safe or escalates to a named human.
Review timeout logs monthly with the steward who owns the clock.
steps: Inventory every state a request can occupy and set a maximum duration for each.
Wire expiry to a fail-safe resolution or a human escalation with a named owner.
Show the declared duration in the interface and log every breach for monthly review.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-04 The Hard Clock)
- Every automated process declares a maximum duration and a human escalation path when it is exceeded.
- Expired processes fail safe and preserve user state for re-entry.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/hard-clock
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-04)
- The declared maximum duration is visible before a person commits to the process.
- Timeout events emit a receipt with the state, elapsed time, and escalation owner.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-04)
[ ] Each system state has a documented maximum duration.
[ ] Timeout logs record expiry, resolution, and escalation owner.
[ ] Monthly reviews are completed by the named steward.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-04)
Trigger review when a state exceeds its declared duration without failing safe or escalating.

artifacts.name: Specification sheet
artifacts.purpose: The full MEC-04 sheet with the definition, the violation, and the spec at /mechanisms/mec-04-hard-clock.

artifacts.name: Facilitation script (PDF)
artifacts.purpose: Workshop script for setting durations with delivery and support teams, at /assets/mec-04-hard-clock-facilitation-script.pdf.

artifacts.name: Timeout log
artifacts.purpose: Record of expiries, resolutions, and escalations for the monthly steward review.

example.title: Bounding a manual review queue
example.description: A payments team caps identity review at 72 hours, shows the cap at submission, and routes anything still pending at expiry to a named reviewer who must release or refuse the hold.

antiPatterns.title: Pending with no ceiling
antiPatterns.failure: A state has a target but no maximum, so slow cases accumulate with no escalation.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Every state declares a maximum duration and a resolution at expiry.
antiPatterns.warning: Targets and maximums can differ; publish both rather than replacing one with the other.

antiPatterns.title: Clock without a resolution
antiPatterns.failure: The timer expires and emits an alert, but the request stays in the same state.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Expiry moves the request to a fail-safe outcome or a named human.
antiPatterns.warning: Escalation counts as a resolution only when the escalation owner can change the state.

entries.title: MEC-05 Kill switch for runaway automation
entries.summary: Pre-authorized halt paths with named stewards, thresholds, and restoration drills so harms stop in seconds.
cues: Define triggers tied to moral performance indicators and frontline reports.
Name the people who can fire the switch and protect them from retaliation.
Rehearse rollbacks so halts land in reversible, well-communicated states.
steps: Map the automation path and mark where halts must land safely with owners.
Set tripwires for ethical interrupts that align with time-to-halt targets.
Run drills that practice firing, communicating, and restoring from the halt.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-05 Kill switch for runaway automation)
- Maintain a pre-authorized halt path with a named roster and protection from retaliation.
- Publish tripwires tied to moral performance indicators and time-to-halt targets.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/kill-switch
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-05)
- The kill switch is reachable within one operational step from monitoring dashboards.
- Halt events emit receipts with owner, trigger, and restoration checklist links.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-05)
[ ] Kill switch runbook names authorized operators and triggers.
[ ] Drill logs demonstrate time-to-halt performance.
[ ] Rollback checklists show safe restoration steps.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-05)
Trigger review when time-to-halt targets are exceeded or the kill switch is unavailable.

artifacts.name: Kill switch runbook
artifacts.purpose: Documents triggers, authorized operators, and post-halt messaging.

artifacts.name: Rollback checklist
artifacts.purpose: Confirms data, access, and user impact are stable before resuming.

artifacts.name: After-action log template
artifacts.purpose: Captures what tripped the switch and how to tighten thresholds or observability.

example.title: Containing a runaway recommendation loop
example.description: Operations staff notice a spike in appeals and trip the kill switch, freezing recommendations, routing cases to humans, and restoring with updated thresholds before re-enabling automation.

antiPatterns.title: Kill switch without rehearsal
antiPatterns.failure: A halt path exists but no drills confirm that it works under pressure.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Teams rehearse halts and document restore steps with time-to-halt targets.
antiPatterns.warning: Simulation is acceptable when production drills are risky, but it must be documented.

antiPatterns.title: Single-point approval
antiPatterns.failure: Only one person can trigger the halt, creating dead zones off-hours.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: A pre-authorized roster can halt automation without retaliation risk.
antiPatterns.warning: Small teams can assign a primary/secondary if coverage is explicit.

entries.title: MEC-06 Appeal paths inside the UI
entries.summary: Give people a built-in channel to dispute outputs, get human review, or learn how a decision was made.
cues: Explain who reviews appeals and the expected response time.
Pre-fill context to reduce effort during stressful moments.
Track appeal outcomes to improve signal credibility.
steps: Place an appeal entry point near the affected decision with response times.
Pre-fill context so people can submit without rebuilding the story.
Track outcomes and feed them back into product and policy updates.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-06 Appeal paths inside the UI)
- Provide an in-product appeal channel with published response timelines.
- Log appeal outcomes and feed them into governance review cycles.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/appeal-paths
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-06)
- Every appeal submission generates a receipt with response timeline and owner.
- Appeals are accessible from the decision surface without extra navigation.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-06)
[ ] Appeal intake form includes pre-filled context.
[ ] Reviewer rota and escalation paths are documented.
[ ] Outcome log tracks response times and resolutions.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-06)
Trigger review when appeal backlogs breach published response timelines.

artifacts.name: Appeal intake form
artifacts.purpose: Collects the minimum details with pre-filled context from the UI.

artifacts.name: Reviewer rota
artifacts.purpose: Lists who reviews appeals, coverage hours, and escalation paths.

artifacts.name: Outcome log
artifacts.purpose: Keeps decisions, response times, and fixes visible to teams and leadership.

example.title: Adding appeals to a risk scoring tool
example.description: The team adds an on-screen “Dispute this score” link with expected response times, routes submissions to a staffed rota, and logs turnaround data to improve credibility with regulators.

antiPatterns.title: Appeal link buried
antiPatterns.failure: Appeals exist but are hidden in help docs or separate portals far from the decision.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Appeal entry points sit next to the affected decision with visible timelines.
antiPatterns.warning: Low-frequency contexts can use a help center if it is still clear and accessible.

antiPatterns.title: Appeals without feedback
antiPatterns.failure: Collects disputes but provides no receipt, timeline, or outcome signal.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Every appeal generates a receipt, timeline, and outcome log.
antiPatterns.warning: Timelines can vary by case complexity if the variance is stated and tracked.

entries.title: MEC-07 Accountability latency tracker
entries.summary: Measure how quickly teams can intervene, halt, and restore systems when accountability is on the line.
cues: Instrument veto, halt, and restore events with owner and trigger metadata.
Publish accountability latency targets alongside time-to-halt SLAs.
Tie latency deltas to post-incident repair log entries.
Feed latency observations into the transition rules on authority grants, so a breach can move a grant to review_required.
steps: Define the telemetry contract for veto, halt, and restoration events.
Surface a dashboard that shows median latency and breach incidents.
Review latency drift during governance reviews and update runbooks.
Wire breach events to the grant transition rules in the authority grant register so an observation can change the governing state.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-07 Accountability latency tracker)
- Track veto, halt, and restore latencies with owner, trigger, and system context.
- Publish accountability latency targets in incident response runbooks.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/accountability-latency-tracker
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-07)
- Monitoring dashboards show accountability latency alongside time-to-halt metrics.
- Veto events emit receipts linked to the repair log and designated escalation owners.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-07)
[ ] Telemetry captures veto, halt, and restore events with timestamps.
[ ] Dashboards report median and worst-case accountability latency.
[ ] Incident reviews include latency deltas and corrective actions.
[ ] Latency breaches are wired to grant transitions and produce a reconsideration record.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-07)
Trigger review when accountability latency breaches published targets or telemetry is missing.

artifacts.name: Telemetry contract
artifacts.purpose: Defines event names, required fields, and tags for observability tooling.

artifacts.name: Dashboard snapshot
artifacts.purpose: Shares latency trends and breach annotations for governance reviews.

artifacts.name: Latency response runbook
artifacts.purpose: Outlines response owners, escalation paths, and remediation steps.

example.title: Tracking veto response time during an incident
example.description: Operations teams add veto latency tracking to their Datadog dashboards, review weekly deltas, and tie missed targets to repair log updates and training.

antiPatterns.title: Latency tracked without owners
antiPatterns.failure: Metrics exist, but no one is accountable for acting on latency breaches.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Dashboards list named owners and escalation paths for each latency tier.
antiPatterns.warning: Shared ownership works when escalation paths are explicit and rehearsed.

antiPatterns.title: Telemetry without repair links
antiPatterns.failure: Latency events are logged but never tied to remediation plans.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Every breach links to a repair log entry with follow-up actions.
antiPatterns.warning: If the repair log lives elsewhere, provide a canonical cross-link.

entries.title: MEC-08 Contestation APIs
entries.summary: Expose programmatic interfaces that let affected people challenge decisions and trigger binding state changes.
cues: Publish a stable API contract that documents inputs, owners, and response timelines.
Return receipts with contest IDs, status, and escalation paths on submission.
Require binding authority to update system state when contests are upheld.

Carry the standing-register fields in the contract: who may challenge, what they may challenge, admissible evidence, the obliged responder, the deadline, the standard of review, and the transitions a successful challenge can produce.
steps: Define an authenticated contestation endpoint with required evidence fields.
Emit status updates via webhooks or receipts tied to the decision record.
Link contest outcomes to state-change logs and remedy tracking.
Publish the standing register alongside the API so a challenger can see the responder, deadline, standard of review, and possible state transitions before filing.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-08 Contestation APIs)
- Publish a contestation API with binding authority and response timelines.
- Ensure contest outcomes can trigger state changes without manual re-entry.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/contestation-apis
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-08)
- Each contest submission returns a receipt with owner, SLA clock, and escalation path.
- Contest outcomes update the decision state and notify the impacted party.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-08)
[ ] API contract and auth policy are documented and versioned.
[ ] Receipts include timestamps, owners, and escalation metadata.
[ ] State-change logs link contest outcomes to remediation steps.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-08)
Trigger review when contest outcomes fail to update system state within the SLA.

artifacts.name: Contestation API spec
artifacts.purpose: Defines endpoints, required fields, and receipt payloads.

artifacts.name: Receipt + webhook schema
artifacts.purpose: Standardizes status updates and escalation metadata for contested decisions.

artifacts.name: State-change log
artifacts.purpose: Links contest outcomes to decision reversals and remedy actions.

artifacts.name: Standing register
artifacts.purpose: Who may challenge what, with admissible evidence, obliged responder, deadline, standard of review, and possible transitions.

example.title: Appeal API for eligibility reversals
example.description: A benefits platform ships an appeal API that accepts structured evidence, returns a receipt with a 72-hour SLA, and automatically updates eligibility state when reviewers reverse the decision.

antiPatterns.title: Contest intake without state change
antiPatterns.failure: Contests are accepted but never mutate the underlying decision state.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Contestation outcomes are wired directly to state-change workflows.
antiPatterns.warning: Manual overrides are acceptable only when logs prove timely updates.

antiPatterns.title: Channel without standing
antiPatterns.failure: The API accepts submissions but never says who is entitled to a response, by when, or against what standard it will be judged.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: The contract names the responder, the deadline, the standard of review, and the transitions a successful challenge can produce.
antiPatterns.warning: A broad standing rule is fine; leaving standing unstated is not.

entries.title: MEC-09 Burden dashboards
entries.summary: Make user burden visible with dashboards that track time, steps, and escalation effort across cohorts.
cues: Publish burden metrics alongside outcome and SLA dashboards.
Segment burden by cohort, channel, and escalation tier.
Flag burden spikes as governance incidents with owners.
steps: Define burden signals (time, steps, waiting, handoffs) and thresholds.
Build a dashboard view with cohort breakdowns and trend lines.
Review burden deltas during governance or product reviews.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-09 Burden dashboards)
- Publish burden metrics and thresholds for high-impact systems.
- Assign owners to remediate burden spikes within a defined window.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/burden-dashboards
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-09)
- Dashboards report median and tail burden metrics by cohort.
- Burden alerts trigger a remediation task with accountable owners.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-09)
[ ] Burden signals are defined and logged consistently.
[ ] Dashboards include cohort breakdowns and escalation visibility.
[ ] Remediation actions are tracked against burden alerts.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-09)
Trigger review when burden thresholds are exceeded without remediation.

artifacts.name: Burden metric spec
artifacts.purpose: Defines calculation inputs and thresholds for burden tracking.

artifacts.name: Dashboard snapshot
artifacts.purpose: Shows burden trends by cohort and escalation tier.

artifacts.name: Burden remediation log
artifacts.purpose: Tracks actions taken to reduce burden spikes.

example.title: Publishing a monthly burden readout
example.description: A city services portal ships a burden dashboard that highlights time spent per appeal, escalations required, and targeted reductions quarter over quarter.

antiPatterns.title: Burden tracking without action
antiPatterns.failure: Teams measure burden but do not assign remediation owners.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Burden alerts route to named owners with fix timelines.
antiPatterns.warning: Small teams can use rotating ownership if coverage is clear.

entries.title: MEC-10 Reversibility audit logs
entries.summary: Track which actions can be reversed, how long reversal takes, and why irreversibility exists.
cues: Document reversibility status and rationale for every high-impact action.
Log reversal attempts with time-to-restore metrics.
Surface irreversibility as a risk flag in governance reviews.
steps: Tag actions with reversibility status and documented rationale.
Log every reversal attempt with timestamps and outcome.
Review irreversibility trends and update mitigation plans.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-10 Reversibility audit logs)
- Maintain an audit log that tracks reversibility status and rationale.
- Record reversal attempts with time-to-restore outcomes.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/reversibility-audit-logs
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-10)
- Decision records display reversibility status and owner.
- Reversal attempts emit receipts with timestamps and outcomes.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-10)
[ ] Reversibility status is captured for high-impact actions.
[ ] Reversal attempts are logged with time-to-restore metrics.
[ ] Irreversibility rationale is documented and reviewed.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-10)
Trigger review when reversibility logs are missing or reversal attempts exceed targets.

artifacts.name: Reversibility status registry
artifacts.purpose: Lists actions with reversibility status, owners, and rationales.

artifacts.name: Reversal attempt log
artifacts.purpose: Tracks reversal attempts, outcomes, and time-to-restore metrics.

artifacts.name: Irreversibility review memo
artifacts.purpose: Summarizes irreversibility rationale and mitigation commitments.

example.title: Logging reversal attempts in a claims system
example.description: A healthcare claims team logs every reversal attempt, including time-to-restore and irreversibility rationale, and reviews the audit log quarterly.

antiPatterns.title: Implicit irreversibility
antiPatterns.failure: Actions are treated as irreversible without documenting why.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Reversibility status and rationale are explicit and reviewed.
antiPatterns.warning: Short-term irreversibility is acceptable if mitigations are documented.

entries.title: MEC-11 Escalation SLAs
entries.summary: Guarantee response times for human escalation when automated decisions are contested.
cues: Publish escalation clocks with named owners and coverage windows.
Tie escalation SLAs to staffing plans and on-call rosters.
Trigger safe-mode or reversal when escalation SLAs are breached.
steps: Define escalation tiers with SLA targets and authority scopes.
Instrument SLA tracking with receipts and breach alerts.
Review breach trends and adjust staffing or automation guardrails.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-11 Escalation SLAs)
- Publish escalation response time guarantees and owners.
- Define breach actions that trigger safe-mode or reversal.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/escalation-slas
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-11)
- Escalation receipts include SLA targets and responsible owners.
- SLA breaches trigger automatic fallback or halt actions.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-11)
[ ] Escalation SLAs and owners are published.
[ ] Breach alerts and fallback actions are logged.
[ ] Staffing plans map to escalation coverage requirements.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-11)
Trigger review when escalation SLA breaches exceed thresholds.

artifacts.name: Escalation SLA matrix
artifacts.purpose: Lists tiers, response targets, and authority scopes.

artifacts.name: Coverage roster
artifacts.purpose: Shows staffing coverage aligned to SLA commitments.

artifacts.name: Breach response log
artifacts.purpose: Tracks SLA breaches and fallback actions.

example.title: 24-hour escalation guarantee for disputes
example.description: A financial platform publishes a 24-hour human escalation SLA for contested denials and routes breaches into automatic provisional reinstatement.

antiPatterns.title: Escalation without coverage
antiPatterns.failure: Escalation timelines exist but no staffing covers nights or weekends.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Coverage rosters align with published escalation SLAs.
antiPatterns.warning: Limited hours are acceptable if clearly disclosed and mitigated.

entries.title: MEC-12 Stoppability testing
entries.summary: Verify pre-deployment that systems can be halted by authorized stakeholders under defined conditions.
cues: Run stoppability drills before launch and after major changes.
Document who can halt, how, and the expected time-to-halt.
Log stoppability test outcomes and remediation actions.
steps: Define stoppability test scenarios with triggers and owners.
Execute drills that measure time-to-halt and safe restoration.
Publish test results and close gaps before release.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-12 Stoppability testing)
- Require stoppability drills before launch and after major changes.
- Publish time-to-halt targets and authorized halt owners.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/stoppability-testing
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-12)
- Stoppability tests log time-to-halt and restoration outcomes.
- Launch gates verify test completion and remediation.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-12)
[ ] Drill logs include time-to-halt metrics and outcomes.
[ ] Authorized halt owners are documented.
[ ] Remediation actions are tracked to closure.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-12)
Trigger review when stoppability tests are skipped or time-to-halt targets are missed.

artifacts.name: Stoppability test plan
artifacts.purpose: Defines scenarios, triggers, and expected time-to-halt targets.

artifacts.name: Drill log
artifacts.purpose: Records stoppability test outcomes and restoration steps.

artifacts.name: Launch gate checklist
artifacts.purpose: Confirms stoppability tests are complete before deployment.

example.title: Pre-launch halt drill for automated approvals
example.description: A public benefits team runs a stoppability drill before release, measuring time-to-halt and verifying restoration steps before approving launch.

antiPatterns.title: Stoppability assumed, not tested
antiPatterns.failure: Teams rely on documentation without running drills.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Stoppability drills run on a calendar and log outcomes.
antiPatterns.warning: Simulated drills are acceptable if production tests are risky.

entries.title: MEC-13 Authority grant register
entries.summary: Hold every delegated authority as a stateful record with provenance, scope, evidence basis, expiry, revocation conditions, and state history.
cues: Give each grant a state, not a boolean: proposed, allowed, review_required, suspended, revoked.
Record what the grant rests on, who issued it, and what would end it.
Expose the register to the decision log so an action can name the grant it ran under.
steps: Enumerate the authorities the system currently exercises and write one record per grant.
Add provenance, scope, evidence basis, expiry, and revocation conditions to each record.
Append every state change to the grant's history and link the register to the decision log.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-13 Authority grant register)
- Maintain a register of delegated authorities with issuer, scope, evidence basis, expiry, and revocation conditions.
- Record every grant state change with its reason and reviewer, and expose the register to the decision log.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/authority-grant-register
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-13)
- Each consequential action names the grant identifier and grant state it ran under.
- Grants past expiry move to review_required and are refused until a reviewer renews them.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-13)
[ ] Every exercised authority has a register entry with issuer and scope.
[ ] Grants carry an expiry and stated revocation conditions.
[ ] State history shows who changed each grant and on what basis.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-13)
Trigger review when an action runs under a grant that is missing, expired, or not in the allowed state.

artifacts.name: Grant record template
artifacts.purpose: Fields for issuer, holder, scope, evidence basis, expiry, revocation conditions, and state.

artifacts.name: State transition table
artifacts.purpose: The permitted moves between grant states and who may make each one.

artifacts.name: Renewal calendar
artifacts.purpose: Upcoming expiries with the reviewer responsible for each renewal decision.

example.title: Registering an agent's refund authority
example.description: A support platform records the agent's refund authority as a grant with a value ceiling, an evidence basis in the last accuracy review, a 90-day expiry, and revocation on any confirmed mis-refund; the refund endpoint reads the grant state before acting.

antiPatterns.title: Permissions as config
antiPatterns.failure: Authority lives in a role file or feature flag with no issuer, basis, or expiry, so widening it is a deploy rather than a decision.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Authority lives in a register where each grant names its issuer, basis, expiry, and revocation conditions.
antiPatterns.warning: Config can still enforce the grant; the register is the record of why the config says what it says.

antiPatterns.title: Register without state
antiPatterns.failure: Grants are documented once and never move, so an expired or contested grant reads the same as a current one.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Each grant carries a current state and an appended history of transitions.
antiPatterns.warning: A stable grant is fine; what matters is that the register can show it was reviewed and left in place.

entries.title: MEC-14 Policy review triggers
entries.summary: Treat policy as state by giving every policy record an expiry and named triggers that move dependent grants to review when the world changes.
cues: Write down the propositions a policy assumes, not only the rule it states.
Name the observation that should reopen the policy, and the threshold that counts.
Link each policy to the grants that rest on it so a fired trigger can reach them.
steps: Give each policy a version, an assumption list, an expiry, and named review triggers.
Link grants to the policies they depend on so the dependency is queryable.
On a fired trigger or a passed expiry, move dependent grants to review_required and notify the reviewer.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-14 Policy review triggers)
- Every policy record carries a version, stated assumptions, an expiry, and named review triggers.
- A fired trigger or a passed expiry moves dependent authority grants to review_required.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/policy-review-triggers
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-14)
- Policy records expose the grants that depend on them and the triggers that reopen them.
- Trigger events emit a reconsideration record with the observation that fired them.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-14)
[ ] Each policy states its assumptions, expiry, and review triggers.
[ ] Grant-to-policy links are recorded and current.
[ ] Fired triggers show the resulting grant state changes and reviewer decisions.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-14)
Trigger review when a material change in the evidence left the policy and its dependent grants untouched.

artifacts.name: Policy record template
artifacts.purpose: Version, assumptions, evidence, expiry, triggers, and dependent grants in one record.

artifacts.name: Trigger catalog
artifacts.purpose: The observations and thresholds that reopen a policy, with the owner of each.

artifacts.name: Reconsideration log
artifacts.purpose: What fired, which grants moved, who reviewed, and what was decided.

example.title: Reopening an eligibility rule after a population shift
example.description: A benefits team gives its eligibility policy a 12-month expiry and a trigger on a five-point shift in applicant mix; when the shift lands, the two grants that cite the policy move to review_required and the reviewer renews one and narrows the other.

antiPatterns.title: Policy as ground truth
antiPatterns.failure: The policy is treated as a fixed input consumed at deployment, so changed facts never reach the authority that rests on it.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Policy is a versioned state with assumptions, expiry, and triggers that can move grants.
antiPatterns.warning: A policy can be long-lived; what it may not be is unreviewable.

antiPatterns.title: Triggers with no destination
antiPatterns.failure: Alerts fire on the metric but nothing in the authority state changes.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: A fired trigger moves the dependent grants and produces a reconsideration record.
antiPatterns.warning: A reviewer may leave the grant in place; the record of that decision is the point.

entries.title: MEC-15 Withdrawal rehearsal
entries.summary: Run the workflow without the system on a schedule and measure what withdrawal would actually cost at the technical, operational, and institutional levels.
cues: Rehearse the workflow without the system rather than testing that the switch flips.
Measure cost, the expertise still available, and time to restore at each reversibility level.
Record which capacities have to be preserved to keep the rehearsal possible next year.
steps: Pick a bounded slice of the workflow and run it without the system for a defined window.
Record the cost, the people who still hold the expertise, and the time to restore service at the technical, operational, and institutional levels.
Publish the gaps as preserved capacities with owners and a date for the next rehearsal.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-15 Withdrawal rehearsal)
- Rehearse operating the workflow without the system on a published schedule.
- Record cost, expertise available, and time to restore at the technical, operational, and institutional levels.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/withdrawal-rehearsal
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-15)
- The system supports a rehearsal mode that suspends automated handling for a defined scope and window.
- Rehearsal outcomes are recorded against the dependency record for the workflow.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-15)
[ ] Rehearsals ran on schedule with a defined scope and window.
[ ] Results state cost, expertise available, and time to restore at all three levels.
[ ] Preserved capacities have named owners and review dates.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-15)
Trigger review when a rehearsal is skipped, or when it shows the workflow can no longer be run without the system.

artifacts.name: Rehearsal plan
artifacts.purpose: Scope, window, participants, and the measures to be taken during the exercise.

artifacts.name: Three-level reversibility readout
artifacts.purpose: Cost and time to restore recorded separately for technical, operational, and institutional withdrawal.

artifacts.name: Preserved capacity list
artifacts.purpose: The staffing, tooling, and knowledge that must be maintained for withdrawal to stay possible, with owners.

example.title: A week of manual triage
example.description: A claims team runs one region manually for a week each quarter, finds that throughput halves and that only two reviewers still hold the rules, and funds a training rotation as a preserved capacity.

antiPatterns.title: The switch exists
antiPatterns.failure: A documented kill switch is treated as proof of reversibility, though nobody has run the workflow without the system in years.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Withdrawal is rehearsed on a schedule and the cost of doing it is measured.
antiPatterns.warning: A rehearsal can be scoped to a slice of traffic; what it may not be is hypothetical.

antiPatterns.title: Rehearsal without a record
antiPatterns.failure: The drill happens but produces no measurement, so nothing can be compared to last year.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Each rehearsal records cost, expertise, and restore time against the dependency record.
antiPatterns.warning: Qualitative findings are useful, but at least one comparable measure has to survive the exercise.

entries.title: MEC-16 Intervention specification
entries.summary: Replace the human-in-the-loop checkbox with a specification of who intervenes, what they can see, what they can prevent or alter, and what happens when they disagree.
cues: State what the intervener can see at the moment of the decision, not afterwards.
Separate what they can prevent from what they can alter after the fact.
Write down what happens when the human disagrees with the system.
steps: Name the intervention owner and the decisions they cover.
Record the information available, the actions preventable, the states alterable, and the on-disagreement path.
Record the incentives acting on the intervener, the cost of intervening, and the time it takes them to reach the decision.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-16 Intervention specification)
- Any control described as human oversight is documented as an intervention specification with owner, information available, actions preventable, states alterable, and on-disagreement path.
- The specification records the incentives, the cost of intervening, and the time to reach the decision.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/intervention-specification
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-16)
- The interface presents the intervener with the information the specification names, before the action commits.
- Disagreement is a recorded outcome with a route, not an unlogged override.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-16)
[ ] Every claimed oversight control has a current intervention specification.
[ ] Reach time and cost of intervening are measured, not asserted.
[ ] Disagreement outcomes are logged with what changed as a result.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-16)
Trigger review when a decision described as human-reviewed proceeded without the reviewer being able to alter it.

artifacts.name: Intervention specification template
artifacts.purpose: Owner, information, preventable actions, alterable states, disagreement path, incentives, cost, and reach time.

artifacts.name: Reach-time measurement
artifacts.purpose: Observed time between the trigger and the intervener being in a position to act.

artifacts.name: Disagreement log
artifacts.purpose: Cases where the intervener disagreed, what route it took, and what changed.

example.title: Specifying review on an automated suspension
example.description: A trust and safety team documents that the on-call reviewer sees the evidence and the account history, can prevent suspension for 30 minutes, can reverse it for 14 days, and that disagreement routes to a policy owner within one business day.

antiPatterns.title: Rubber-stamp review
antiPatterns.failure: A human approves in bulk without the information or the time to alter the outcome, and the approval is counted as oversight.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: The specification states what the reviewer sees, what they can change, and how long they have.
antiPatterns.warning: High approval rates are not proof of rubber-stamping; the test is whether refusal was possible and reachable.

antiPatterns.title: Oversight named but not scoped
antiPatterns.failure: Policy says a human is in the loop without saying which decisions, which states, or which disagreement path.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Each oversight claim resolves to a specification covering named decisions.
antiPatterns.warning: One specification can cover a class of decisions if the class is stated.

entries.title: MEC-17 Capability catalog
entries.summary: Keep a discovery surface separate from the grant register so a system can reason about what it could do without being empowered to do it.
cues: Let discovery answer what is possible; let the grant register answer what is permitted.
Record how each capability was tested, and when.
Refuse an ungranted action by naming the capability and the missing grant.
steps: Catalog the actions the assembled system can perform, including those reachable through tools and sub-agents.
Record for each capability how it was verified and when that verification expires.
Serve the catalog on a read path that carries no authority, and refuse execution unless a grant is in the allowed state.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-17 Capability catalog)
- Maintain a catalog of what the assembled system can do, separate from the register of what it is permitted to do.
- Discovery of a capability confers no authority; execution requires a grant in the allowed state.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/capability-catalog
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-17)
- Capability discovery succeeds for actions the system cannot lawfully perform.
- A refusal names the capability, the required grant, and the grant's current state.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-17)
[ ] The catalog lists capabilities reachable through tools and sub-agents.
[ ] Each capability records its verification method and date.
[ ] Attempts to execute ungranted capabilities are refused and logged.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-17)
Trigger review when a newly reachable capability was exercised without a grant being issued for it.

artifacts.name: Capability record template
artifacts.purpose: Action, surface, preconditions, verification method, and verification date.

artifacts.name: Discovery endpoint contract
artifacts.purpose: Read-only interface that returns capabilities and their grant status without granting anything.

artifacts.name: Refusal message pattern
artifacts.purpose: Standard wording that cites the capability, the required grant, and its state.

example.title: An agent that can see the payout tool it may not use
example.description: An operations agent discovers the payout tool in the catalog, reads that the matching grant is in review_required, refuses the action citing the grant identifier and state, and files a request for authorization instead.

antiPatterns.title: Discover equals permit
antiPatterns.failure: Anything the system can reach is treated as something it may do, so capability growth silently widens authority.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Discovery and authorization are separate surfaces, and execution checks the grant.
antiPatterns.warning: Hiding a capability is not a substitute for refusing it; a hidden capability that executes is still ungoverned.

antiPatterns.title: Catalog without verification
antiPatterns.failure: Capabilities are listed from documentation, so the catalog describes intent rather than what the system can actually do.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Each entry records how the capability was tested and when.
antiPatterns.warning: Verification can be sampled; the record should say which entries are asserted rather than tested.

entries.title: MEC-18 Dependency ledger
entries.summary: Track who now depends on the system, what substitution would cost, which expertise remains, and which capacities are being preserved to keep withdrawal possible.
cues: Treat dependence as a state variable that moves, not as a background condition.
Record alternatives while they still exist, not once they are gone.
Give every preserved capacity an owner and a budget line.
steps: List the dependents on the workflow, inside and outside the organization.
Record substitution cost, the expertise retained, and the alternatives that still exist, and derive an exposure score.
Name the preserved capacities with owners and review the ledger on the same cadence as the safety case.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-18 Dependency ledger)
- Maintain a dependency ledger with dependents, substitution cost, expertise retained, alternatives, and an exposure score.
- Name the capacities preserved to keep withdrawal possible, each with an owner.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/dependency-ledger
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-18)
- Exposure score and its inputs are reported alongside reliability metrics.
- Changes in dependents or alternatives update the ledger within the review cycle.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-18)
[ ] Dependents are listed with the consequence of an outage for each.
[ ] Substitution cost, expertise retained, and alternatives are recorded and dated.
[ ] Preserved capacities have owners and evidence they are still funded.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-18)
Trigger review when exposure rises materially without a corresponding change in preserved capacity.

artifacts.name: Dependency record template
artifacts.purpose: Dependents, substitution cost, expertise retained, alternatives, and exposure score.

artifacts.name: Exposure score worksheet
artifacts.purpose: How depth of dependence, substitution cost, and correction latency combine into the score.

artifacts.name: Preserved capacity register
artifacts.purpose: Capacities kept alive for withdrawal, with owners, budget, and review dates.

example.title: Ledger for a scheduling system three years in
example.description: A hospital records that two departments have retired their manual rota, that the last two schedulers who could rebuild it retire next year, and funds a documented fallback rota as a preserved capacity.

antiPatterns.title: Reliability as safety
antiPatterns.failure: High uptime is read as low risk, while the institution's ability to work without the system quietly disappears.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Dependence is tracked separately from reliability, with its own score and owners.
antiPatterns.warning: A reliable system can be a safe one; the ledger asks a different question, which is what happens when it is gone.

antiPatterns.title: Ledger without alternatives
antiPatterns.failure: Dependents are recorded but substitutes are never checked, so the entry cannot show when the last alternative disappeared.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Alternatives are re-checked on the review cadence and dated.
antiPatterns.warning: Having no alternative is a legitimate finding as long as it is recorded as one.

entries.title: MEC-19 Expansion review
entries.summary: Make scope growth its own authorization decision, with fresh evidence and a check that correction capacity grew with it.
cues: Treat a successful pilot as a request to expand, not as an approval to expand.
Ask what correction capacity the wider scope needs before the scope moves.
Record expansion as a transition on the grant, with its own evidence.
steps: Define what counts as expansion for this system: new population, new action class, higher ceiling, or lower attendance.
Require an expansion record with the evidence for the wider scope and the correction capacity it will need.
Record the decision as an expansion transition on the grant, or refuse it and say what evidence is missing.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-19 Expansion review)
- Any growth in population, action class, ceiling, or autonomy is authorized as a new decision with its own evidence.
- The decision records whether correction capacity grows with the expanded scope.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/expansion-review
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-19)
- Scope changes are applied through a grant transition, not through configuration drift.
- The grant history distinguishes expansion transitions from renewals.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-19)
[ ] Expansion criteria are defined for the system.
[ ] Each expansion has a record with evidence and a correction-capacity check.
[ ] Grant histories show expansion transitions with reviewers.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-19)
Trigger review when scope grew without an expansion record, or when it grew while correction capacity stayed fixed.

artifacts.name: Expansion record template
artifacts.purpose: Proposed scope change, evidence for it, and the correction capacity it requires.

artifacts.name: Correction capacity check
artifacts.purpose: Comparison of the reviewers, reversal paths, and repair budget before and after the change.

artifacts.name: Expansion criteria list
artifacts.purpose: What counts as expansion for this system, agreed before the first request.

example.title: From one region to all regions
example.description: A pilot that ran well in one region is treated as a request rather than a result: the team files an expansion record, finds the appeals queue would need two more reviewers, funds them, and only then transitions the grant.

antiPatterns.title: The automation ratchet
antiPatterns.failure: Success is taken as its own authorization, so scope only ever widens and never contracts.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Expansion is a decision with evidence, and contraction is an available outcome.
antiPatterns.warning: Fast expansion is fine when each step is a recorded decision with capacity behind it.

antiPatterns.title: Expansion by configuration
antiPatterns.failure: Scope grows through a threshold change or a new tool binding that no one reviews as an authority change.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Scope changes move through a grant transition with a reviewer.
antiPatterns.warning: Routine parameter tuning inside an agreed ceiling is not expansion; crossing the ceiling is.

syllabus.overview: A guided track for teams adopting the mechanisms. Each module links to glossary anchors and specifications you can cite in docs.

modules.title: Orientation
topics: Mechanisms tour and how to use permalinks in specs
Primer on burden, consent, and stewardship
Navigation of governance, design ethics, and policy filters
modules.outcome: Teams can route questions to the right section and cite glossary terms consistently.

modules.title: Field-ready research
topics: Integrating glossary terms into research and field notes
Tagging findings by focus area and diagnostic relevance
Building appeal paths and consent prompts into prototypes
modules.outcome: Practitioners share findings with linked terms and mechanism cues that ship with the work.

modules.title: Governance and maintenance
topics: Decision logs, stewardship windows, and escalation readiness
Designing safety valves for high-burden scenarios
modules.outcome: Leadership aligns on accountable maintenance plans backed by diagnostic evidence.
